crates/semantic/Cargo.toml:4:version = "0.4.0"
crates/tsc-client/Cargo.toml:4:version = "0.2.1"

* Session only (`createSession`, `initializeSession`, `extractFileIncremental`): parse and index every file, and
   * resolve a component when `sessionDocgenInfo` asks for it (off by default; ADR 0016). `initializeSession` then
   * returns an output with no components.
   */
  lazy?: boolean
  /**
   * Session only: `'on-demand'` asks the built-in TypeScript 7.1 checker for each component a request names, and
   * answers with the structural props when the checker is slower than `semanticWaitMs` (experimental; ADR 0022).
   * `'off'` (the default) never starts it.
   */
  semanticTypes?: 'off' | 'on-demand'
  /**
   * Session only, with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`: a checker binary to run instead of the built-in one
   * (`typescript@7.1`'s `tsc`, or `tsrs`).
   */
  tscPath?: string
  /**
   * Session only, with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`: how many milliseconds a request waits for the checker before
   * it takes the structural answer (default 150).
   */
  semanticWaitMs?: number
  /**
   * Session only, with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`: how many milliseconds a request waits for the checker when the
   * structural pass lists no props for the component (default 2000). A value below `semanticWaitMs` gives such a
   * component `semanticWaitMs`.
   */
  semanticWaitEmptyMs?: number
}

/**
 * The tsconfigs, `package.json` files and lockfiles above the session's source directories: a watcher adds them, and

/**
 * Resolves `count` components spread evenly over the session's keys, without returning them: a lazy session then
 * holds the dependency declarations and resolver memos that components share, so the first request a host answers
 * does not load them. With `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` it asks the checker for each at background priority, after any
 * story someone opened, and does not wait for it: the answers are kept for the stories that follow. Runs off the
 * calling thread and returns how many components it resolved. An eager session, an unknown session and a count of 0
 * resolve nothing.

  srcDirs?: string[]
  exclude?: string[]
  tsconfigPath?: string
  /** Leave out the HTML attributes a component inherits from its element. Same as `htmlAttributes: 'none'`. */
  skipHtmlProps?: boolean
  /**
   * Which HTML attributes a component inherits from its element to list: `'full'` (all of them, the default),
   * `'curated'` (a compact subset: handlers, `aria-*`, `ref`, common attributes) or `'none'`. Wins over `skipHtmlProps`.
   */
  htmlAttributes?: 'curated' | 'full' | 'none'
  /**
   * Read and write the on-disk caches under `node_modules/.cache`. Default: `true`; `false` reads and writes nothing
   * there and parses everything every run. The output is the same.
   */
  cache?: boolean
  /**
   * Load the type declarations your props reference from installed packages, so props typed by a library resolve
   * instead of degrading. Default: `true`; `false` skips the extra work.
   */
  loadDependencies?: boolean
  /**
   * Which inherited sources of more than 30 props to list as one inherited layer instead of prop by prop. Default:
   * `'none'`, every inherited prop listed.
   */
  collapseInheritedProps?: 'dependencies' | 'all' | 'none'
  /**
   * Resolve a component when a story asks for it instead of every component when Storybook starts. Default: `true`.
   * The props are the same; the session starts sooner and holds only the components your stories use.
   */
  lazy?: boolean
  /**
   * With a lazy session, resolve a few components in the background after it starts. Default: `false`: it did not
   * make the first story faster in measurement.
   */
  warmUp?: boolean
  /**
   * With a lazy session, once this many distinct components have been asked for, resolve all the rest in the
   * background in one parallel pass. It lowers the median story latency of a project read end to end (Spectrum's
   * 50 stories: 19 ms to 5 ms) but not the total time, and raises peak memory by 170 to 420 MB, so it is off by
   * default: `0`.
   */
  fillAfter?: number
  /**
   * When the dev server starts, document the components of this many first stories through Storybook's docgen
   * service, before a browser asks. Default: `1`, the story Storybook opens. `0` waits for the browser.
   */
  prefetchStories?: number
  /**
   * Ask the built-in TypeScript 7.1 checker for each component a story names (experimental). `'off'` (the default)
   * never starts it. `'on-demand'` keeps it warm in the background, asks it for exactly the requested component, and
   * uses the structural props when it is slower than `semanticWaitMs`; its answer is kept for the next request.
   */
  semanticTypes?: 'off' | 'on-demand'
  /** A checker binary to run instead of the built-in one: `typescript@7.1`'s `tsc`, or `tsrs`. */
  tscPath?: string

  semanticWaitMs?: number

   * component (a `ComponentProps<typeof Button>` of a library it cannot read), since there is nothing to show before

  semanticWaitEmptyMs?: number

  fallback?: 'degraded' | 'never'

packages/storybook/README.md:44:| `prefetchStories` | `1` | When `storybook dev` starts, document the components of this many first stories through Storybook's docgen service before a browser asks, one after another. That starts the session (and the checker), and stores the opening story's answer where the browser reads it: with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, Chakra's `Button` had the checker's props in the browser before it asked, where they arrived 0.7 to 2.9 s after its request without. The browser still asks the provider again, which answers from the session. A story opened while a prefetch runs waits for it, so a larger number only pays off when the browser opens later than the components take. `0` waits for the browser. |
packages/storybook/README.md:45:| `semanticTypes` | `'off'` | Experimental. `'on-demand'` keeps the built-in TypeScript 7.1 checker warm and asks it for the component a story shows, so props only the type checker can see appear (shadcn's components gain more than twice as many). A story waits up to `semanticWaitMs` for it and otherwise shows the usual props; the checker's answer is kept for the next request. The checker answers the stories you open before `warmUp` and `fillAfter` work, and a story whose component it is already answering waits for that answer instead of asking again. Nothing to install: the checker is part of the addon's native binding. |

1	# Status
2	
3	**Updated:** 2026-11-02
4	
5	Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, watch mode (including rebuilds on config changes and polling with `ensure_fresh`), plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, and bounded atomic DTS caching are implemented and verified.
6	
7	**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. Checked against RDT on five installed repos, loading reports far more of RDT's props and changes 11 matching types in 59,000. Chakra, the worst case, costs about 220 ms and 330 MiB against 50 ms and 100 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`).
8	
9	## Numbers
10	
11	- Rust tests (`cargo nextest` across the workspace, plus the NAPI binding tests) and vitest (unit with a mocked binding, integration against the real native binding), all green in CI
12	- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
13	- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
14	- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded: the share of RDT's reference components and props that Caliper also reports, not a measure of correctness (the checker judges that; on the props both list, the checker contradicts Caliper on 0 to 1.09% and RDT on 0.006 to 5.02%, `docs/rdt-differences.md`, 2026-11-06). The weekly record and the current definition of the reference are in `docs/measurement.md`.
15	- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
16	- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. No pull-request gate enforces it: a weekly workflow records speed, memory and recall against RDT and react-docgen and opens an issue on a worsening, and `just bench` compares a branch with `main` locally (`docs/measurement.md`).
17	
18	## Features and improvements
19	
20	- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
21	- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
22	- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
23	- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
24	- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap. Keyed by content hash, and discarded whenever the build that wrote it differs.
25	- **Lazy sessions** (ADR 0016) — `WatchSession::lazy` parses and indexes every file and resolves a component when a request names it; the Storybook addon uses it by default (NAPI `lazy`, off by default). Each answer equals the batch extraction's for the same key. Numbers in `docs/performance.md`.
26	- **Dependency declarations loaded by default** (ADR 0010) — a prop typed by an installed package resolves; `--no-load-dependencies` turns it off.
27	- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all five crates — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).
28	
29	## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker
30	
31	See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).
32	
33	An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A session can also ask a warm checker for just the component a story requests (`semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, ADR 0022): the first answer waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) and takes the structural props if the checker is slower, and the checker's late answer is kept for the next request. The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates; `tscPath` runs a binary instead), and is experimental and off by default. A failed, crashed or timed-out checker falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table. Under ADR 0026 (slices S1 to S4 done) the checker's answer, when it runs, replaces the structural one prop by prop, and a prop it could not read keeps the structural type with `degradedBy`; it becomes the default in S8.
34	
35	## Experiments that didn't pan out
36	
37	**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn (the 1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn quoted then came from a run that no longer reproduces: the weekly record of 2026-11-06 finds 55 checker-only props on shadcn, all `tw`, and `docs/rdt-differences.md` has the current account). So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted, so the routing numbers above cannot be reproduced; the method is the oracle in `docs/measurement.md`.
38	
39	## Where to look next
40	
41	- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
42	- **Where Caliper's types differ from RDT and the checker, and what that costs** → `rdt-differences.md`.
43	- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
44	- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
45	- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`).
46	- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
47	- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

13	- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
14	- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded: the share of RDT's reference components and props that Caliper also reports, not a measure of correctness (the checker judges that; on the props both list, the checker contradicts Caliper on 0 to 1.09% and RDT on 0.006 to 5.02%, `docs/rdt-differences.md`, 2026-11-06). The weekly record and the current definition of the reference are in `docs/measurement.md`.
15	- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
16	- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. No pull-request gate enforces it: a weekly workflow records speed, memory and recall against RDT and react-docgen and opens an issue on a worsening, and `just bench` compares a branch with `main` locally (`docs/measurement.md`).
17	
18	## Features and improvements
19	
20	- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
21	- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
22	- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
23	- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
24	- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap. Keyed by content hash, and discarded whenever the build that wrote it differs.
25	- **Lazy sessions** (ADR 0016) — `WatchSession::lazy` parses and indexes every file and resolves a component when a request names it; the Storybook addon uses it by default (NAPI `lazy`, off by default). Each answer equals the batch extraction's for the same key. Numbers in `docs/performance.md`.
26	- **Dependency declarations loaded by default** (ADR 0010) — a prop typed by an installed package resolves; `--no-load-dependencies` turns it off.
27	- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all five crates — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).
28	
29	## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker
30	
31	See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).
32	
33	An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A session can also ask a warm checker for just the component a story requests (`semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, ADR 0022): the first answer waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) and takes the structural props if the checker is slower, and the checker's late answer is kept for the next request. The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates; `tscPath` runs a binary instead), and is experimental and off by default. A failed, crashed or timed-out checker falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table. Under ADR 0026 (slices S1 to S4 done) the checker's answer, when it runs, replaces the structural one prop by prop, and a prop it could not read keeps the structural type with `degradedBy`; it becomes the default in S8.
34	
35	## Experiments that didn't pan out
36	
37	**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn (the 1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn quoted then came from a run that no longer reproduces: the weekly record of 2026-11-06 finds 55 checker-only props on shadcn, all `tw`, and `docs/rdt-differences.md` has the current account). So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted, so the routing numbers above cannot be reproduced; the method is the oracle in `docs/measurement.md`.
38	
39	## Where to look next
40	
41	- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
42	- **Where Caliper's types differ from RDT and the checker, and what that costs** → `rdt-differences.md`.
43	- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
44	- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
45	- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`).
46	- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
47	- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

And with the default `fallback: 'degraded'`, `ChakraButton` is handed to React's docgen even when the checker answers, because the structural warning that `Button` was not found stays on the answer.
 
+## In-process guards (trail 369 slice 2)
+
+The checker is linked into the process since #438, so a fault in it is the host's (Node, Storybook): an abort ends it and memory the checker holds is the host's. Measured 2026-11-11 on `feat/in-process-guards`, release builds, tsrs crates `0.24.0`, macOS 27.3 on an Apple M5 Max, the harness on mimalloc as the native binding is (`--tsc built-in`, on a copy of `gate-large` under `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/crates-slice-2`).
+
+- **What the memory is.** In process, the host's resident memory cannot stand for the checker's. Asking the 937 components of `gate-large` one at a time, each from the same lazy session, this process grew to 5,365 MiB in process and 4,967 MiB with the checker in a `tsrs` process, sampled every 100 components: 250 to 400 MiB of the difference is the checker, the rest Caliper's own answers, about 5.5 MiB per Chakra component and kept for the session on either route. The checker's own part is read from the one address range `tsrs` carves its arenas from (`tsrs_core::reserve`, `mincore` over it, 6 ms): 42 to 46 MiB for the watch loop below, up to 165 MiB over the 937 components.
+- **Replacing the session does not help.** The same 650 Chakra edits (`memory`): replaced every 64 programs as #438 shipped, peak 514 MiB, still climbing at 2,000 edits (533 MiB, 31 replacements); never replaced, peak 327 MiB, flat from edit 200 on, and 389 at 2,000 edits with the arenas at 46 MiB throughout. A closed session gave back part of its arenas (46 MiB fell to 22 to 37 MiB) and the fresh one parsed every file again. Over the 937 components, replacing every 64 changed nothing (5,332 against 5,365 MiB at 900). The reservation `tsrs` aborts on when exhausted (32 GiB) held 95 MiB in chunks throughout 2,000 edits never replaced, and 108 to 110 MiB over 1,000 replaced every 64 (`TSRS_MEM_SPLIT=1`), so a long session does not run it out.
+- **The rule.** The built-in checker is never replaced. After its first program and every fourth, its arenas are read; past `max_rss_mib` (768 MiB) it stops for the session and every later request keeps its structural answer with a `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning naming the bound (`crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs`, `Upkeep`). A process is replaced as before. A short-lived helper process for the checker was not built: nothing measured here needs one.
+- **Memory past 600 edits** (`gate_harness memory --tsc built-in`): 650 of 650 answers the checker's, none stale, no replacement, peak 343 MiB for the whole process (377 in a second run), arenas 46 MiB, the last answer equal to a fresh session's. **PASS.** The bound exercised (`--max-rss-mib 44`): the checker answered the first 8 edits, was read at 45 MiB, stopped, and the other 642 answers were structural with the bound's warning; the process peaked at 304 MiB and the arenas fell to 22 MiB. **PASS** (the gate requires every answer before the stop to be the checker's and every one after to be structural, with the warning).
+- **Determinism** (`gate_harness determinism --tsc built-in`, each variant a fresh copy of the harness with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` 1, 2 and 4, three runs each, the middle one in reverse): all nine outputs identical, 399,063,798 bytes each; 148 of 150 components the checker's, `MuiPopoverRoot` and `MuiSliderMark` structural in every run, as on the process route. The processes ran 8 to 10, 9 to 13 and 19 threads at 1, 2 and 4. **PASS.**
+- **First answer and watch, in passing.** First answer for `ChakraButton`: median 171 ms (169 to 173, 5 runs), against 277 ms over the pipe: **FAIL** the 150 ms budget, closer. Watch on `ButtonProps`: p50 157.7, p95 162.3, p99 168.5 ms, query alone 98.7 ms (565 ms p95 over the pipe): **FAIL** 25 ms. Own props: p50 5.3, p95 6.3 ms, against 22.6: **PASS**.
+- **Panics.** A panic inside the checker fails the request it came from; the thread then closes the session and ends, and the next request starts a fresh one, as after a crashed process (three, and the checker stays down). A session a panic unwound through is not asked again, so no later answer reads what it left half-built. `tsrs` itself reports one panic as the client's fault (an unknown `moduleResolution`), and that session is kept. Tests: `crates/semantic/src/checker.rs` (`a_panic_ends_the_session_after_answering_its_request_with_the_error`, with a stand-in session that panics, since the one input known to panic `tsrs` 0.24, an unknown `moduleResolution`, is reported as the client's fault).
+- **Stack depth.** `tsrs` parses on its own threads with 256 MiB stacks (`tsrs_compiler::program::worker_pool`), and its checker runs on the 512 MiB `caliper-checker` thread. Nested 50,000 deep, all nine shapes tried parse and print without an abort (an object, generic, `Array`, parenthesis, binary `+`, tuple, arrow and conditional type, and JSX). Past that, a thread of `tsrs`'s own overflows (never `caliper-checker`), which aborts the process: an object type at 300,000 (200,000 parses), a generic at 300,000, a tuple at 500,000 (300,000 parses), JSX at 700,000 (500,000 parses), an arrow chain at 700,000 (500,000 parses), and parentheses and `+` at 1,000,000 (700,000 and 200,000 parse). So the checker is not given a file whose bracket nesting passes 20,000 (`(`, `[` and `{` together, `<` apart): the request that read it fails with a warning naming the file, and its components keep their structural answer. A snapshot that request made (a refused `createSnapshot` or `updateSnapshot`) is released before the error goes back, since its id never reaches the caller; so is one made for a caller that stopped waiting (`checker::tests::a_snapshot_made_by_a_refused_request_is_released_and_the_ones_answered_are_kept`, which fails on `68e9a90e`). The measure costs 5.3 ms for the 4.7 MB of Chakra, Ark, Zag, `@types/react` and `csstype` declarations, whose deepest nesting is 187. Not covered: nesting written without brackets (arrow chains, conditional types, long `+` chains), which overflows only past 500,000. The 10,000-deep test now runs in release in the checker lane.
+- **Linux.** CI's `Test / Rust` job (ubuntu) runs the semantic suite on the built-in checker, so the linked crates build and answer on Linux in every PR and on `main` (green at `8212aef8`, #438 included); the measurements above are macOS only.
+
 ## Not covered
 
 - Other platforms: both measurements ran on macOS arm64. The Linux CI run is a separate gate.

110:A long-lived session (the Storybook addon, the lazy `WatchSession`) can attach a warm checker instead of running the whole-project pass above: `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` (ADR 0022). `caliper-docgen-semantic` keeps one checker warm (the built-in one, or a `tscPath` process) behind a worker thread, answers from a program rooted at only the requested component's file, and returns its props. The program's snapshot is kept between requests and brought up to date with the files the session says changed ("Watch", below). `WatchSession::component` merges them into the structural answer by name (the checker's type wins, a structural prop the checker did not return stays, and `htmlAttributes` applies once after the merge, as in the structural pass) when they arrive within `semanticWaitMs` (default 150 ms), or within `semanticWaitEmptyMs` (default 2,000 ms, never less than `semanticWaitMs`) when the structural answer lists no props at all (a `ComponentProps<typeof Button>` of a package the structural pass does not model, whose props type it could not expand); otherwise it returns the structural answer plus an `Info` diagnostic, and the checker's late answer serves the next request of the same component while no source file has changed. lines: - **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.

- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
-- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` or a config option turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` give way to it.

+- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` (`checker: false` in the config, the napi binding and the Storybook addon) turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` are removed (S8).

- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint was re-measured with tsrs in S4 and holds (Chakra's `Button`, 562 ms, 402 ms after the first-answer work). The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).

- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose; the checker lane's `tsrs` binary (`0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) follows them. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.

- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed. `--tsc-path` (`tscPath`) runs a checker binary as a process instead, which is how the Go `typescript` beta stays the oracle and the parity gate. A checker process is replaced above an RSS threshold (`OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`); the linked checker is replaced by a fresh session after 64 programs, which does not return its memory.

## The checker is the default (S8)

S8 turns the checker on by default (`--no-checker` and `checker: false` turn it off). Measured 2026-11-12 on `feat/checker-is-default` against `main` at `8212aef8`, release builds, the built-in checker (tsrs crates `0.24.0`), macOS 27.3 on an Apple M5 Max, a shared machine at load 8 to 21. Scratch inputs are under `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default`.

- **Whole-project `extract`** (`extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`, otherwise the CLI's defaults; wall time and peak RSS from `time -l`, 3 interleaved runs each, ranges):
  - `gate-large`, 938 Chakra and MUI wrappers: **6.05 to 10.56 s, 966 to 974 MiB** by default (the 10.56 s run was the first, at the highest load; the other two 6.05 s). `--no-checker`: 0.09 to 0.10 s, 201 to 203 MiB. `main` gave 0.09 to 0.10 s and 196 to 198 MiB by default, and 6.18 to 8.33 s and 968 to 973 MiB with `--experimental-semantic-types`.
  - The 787 Chakra wrappers alone: **5.37 to 5.55 s, 765 to 776 MiB** by default; `--no-checker` 0.07 to 0.08 s, 158 MiB; `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` 5.37 to 5.50 s, 759 to 772 MiB.
  - Three renamed copies of `gate-large` (2,814 components, one run): 15.4 s and 1,053 MiB by default, 0.14 s and 228 MiB with `--no-checker`. Memory hardly grows with the component count: the whole-project pass holds one program and interns equal props across components, so no `extract` measured here comes near 2 GB.
  - Output: the default's canonical JSON equals `main`'s `--experimental-semantic-types` once `stats` is set aside, and `--no-checker`'s equals `main`'s default but for one help text (`OPAQUE_TYPE`'s hint now names `--no-checker`).
  - Not measured: the five corpora of `docs/measurement.md`, which are not installed here (no corpus was fetched for this).
- **A session's kept answers** (the Storybook addon's configuration through the native binding: lazy, dependencies loaded, nothing collapsed, `semanticWaitMs` and `semanticWaitEmptyMs` 60 s so every answer is the checker's; `gate-large`'s components asked one at a time, the process's RSS read every 100). Each checker answer is kept for the next request, and each held its own copy of every prop: 1,257, 1,930 and 2,602 MiB after 100, 200 and 300 components, about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component (trail 369 slice 2 read 5,365 MiB at 900). The structural session alone (`checker: false`) peaks at 377 MiB.
- **Budgets, per trail 333.** The first answer keeps its 150 ms budget for a story that was prefetched or answered before (the addon's `prefetchStories`, then the kept answer); the cold first answer is recorded rather than gated: `ChakraButton` median **171 ms** in process (169 to 173, trail 369 slice 2), against 277 ms over the pipe. Watch keeps 25 ms for the checker's own part (own props: p95 6.3 ms in process), and records the `ButtonProps` form: **p95 162.3 ms** (p50 157.7, p99 168.5), whose floor is converting its 1,138 props.

# Semantic backend (TypeScript 7)

**Status:** slice 1 implemented as an experimental opt-in, off by default ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md), [ADR 0007](adr/0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md)): `extract --experimental-semantic-types` (see "Slice 1" below). [ADR 0026](adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md)'s slices S1 to S4 are in: when the checker runs, its answer wins prop by prop (see "The checker's answer wins"); it becomes the default in S8. The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates, see "The checker"); `--tsc-path` runs a binary instead. Structural extraction stays the default and the fallback. Separately, TypeScript 7.1's checker runs as a test-only oracle for structural prop types (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, `docs/measurement.md`). **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 for slice 1 against `7.1.0-beta`; 2026-09-27 for the Cost measurements, each naming its nightly; 2026-10-22 for the API table against the `7.1.0-beta` package; 2026-10-23 for the fixture-corpus parity on `7.1.0-beta`.

## Next step

Slice 1 below covers function components by their export. Next, in order: set what `PropType` now carries (index signatures, `readonly`, a ref type's name; optional and rest parameters are done; per-prop `tags` and `parent` are done, see S7a below), class components (generic ones are read at their default: "Generic components" below), and `batchRequests` to cut round trips; watch-mode notifications are done ("Watch" below). The NAPI binding already ships: a session asks a warm checker for the requested component (`semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, ADR 0022). The client's open Lifecycle items in the Gates table still stand.

Some props can't be resolved from the AST alone. An opt-in backend asks TypeScript's checker instead, using the algorithm react-docgen-typescript (RDT) uses, and merges the answer into the structural result. Structural extraction stays the default.

## What the structural resolver can't do

Component prop counts from `fixtures/` with `--html-attributes full`, against RDT. Root causes are from `docs/benchmarks.md`.

| Gap | Example | Ours | RDT |
| --- | --- | --: | --: |
| Generics through alias chains | ariakit `Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` | 5 | 294 |
| Generics through alias chains | ark-ui `SelectRoot` | 36 | 314 |
| Conditional types | headlessui `PropsOf<TTag>` | 14 | 246 |
| Mapped types over a generic | base-ui `WithBaseUIEvent<T>` | 11 | 293 |
| Conditional type and indexed access | fluentui `Slot<Type, ...>` | 8 | 303 |
| `@emotion/styled` two-argument overload | storybook-emotion `Button` | 7 | 306 |

In the 2026-07-25 baseline, 10 of 33 compared components account for 2,696 of 2,720 missing props. The other 24 are `ref` and `key`, which this tool omits by design (`MIGRATING.md`).

## How it works

```
OXC parse → structural resolver ─────────────────┐
                                                 ├→ merge → ExtractionOutput
tsrs (built in) → semantic resolver (opt-in) ───┘
```

The structural result is complete on its own and returns first. The semantic pass reads each exported component from the checker and replaces the structural props where it finds one.

### Merge rules (proposed)

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Props present, `type`, `required` | Semantic. A `type` the checker could not read (an `opaque` part) where the structural one is read in full stays structural, marked (see "The checker's answer wins") |
| `parent`, `declarations` | Semantic. `declarations` lists every declaring interface, not just the first |
| `description`, `tags` | Semantic JSDoc, structural if empty |
| `composes` | Semantic: the `@types/react` types the props type is made of |
| `defaultValue` | oxc: the component's code (a destructured parameter's initializer, `defaultProps`), else the checker's `@default` tag; structural where neither has one (S7a2) |
| Components tsc doesn't surface (not exported) | Structural only |
| Structural diagnostics of a resolved component | Dropped where the checker's answer supersedes them (see "Diagnostics a checker answer supersedes") |

### What gets dropped, and where

| Dropped | Where | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` without a description | RDT projection only. Canonical keeps it | Done |
| Ambient `.d.ts` components such as `PureComponent` | Merge step | Done |
| `key` | Not emitted, matching the structural path | Closed |
| `ref` | Emitted in `curated` and `full` for `ComponentProps<"div">`-style props and `forwardRef` components, matching the structural path | Closed |
| HTML and DOM attributes in curated and none mode | Semantic adapter, by declaring interface rather than by name | Open |

### Delivery (proposed)

The structural result returns immediately. The semantic result follows: the CLI waits for it behind an opt-in flag, and the NAPI binding exposes a second async call so the Vite plugin can patch when it resolves. Spawn `tsc` at the start of the run so it loads while extraction runs. Each result carries a content hash, and a stale one is dropped.

238	- **Measured** (`extract` with the checker, then behind `--experimental-semantic-types`, with the weekly's options, tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, against the run before this slice). Before, the structural answer gave the order of 2,736 of Spectrum's 3,194 merged union props and 187 of gate-large's 432,813, and every default: on Spectrum 870 from code, 378 `@default` tags the checker also gives, 15 from the resolver only; on gate-large 499 tags. Now, Spectrum: 27 props gain a code default and none loses one; 11 of 3,686 unions change order, each to the written one (`focusMode?: 'child' | 'cell'`, `slot?: string | null`). With `--no-resolver-facts` 15 defaults (the mapped `@default` case above) and 22 more union orders (imported aliases) differ. gate-large: 834 props gain a default (the checker's `@default` tags of props only the checker returns) and none loses one; 1,452 of 432,690 unions take the written order (`translate?: 'yes' | 'no'`, `css`); with `--no-resolver-facts` no default and 16 more union orders differ (members through an import, such as MUI's `timeout?: TransitionProps['timeout'] | 'auto'`).
239	- **Cost.** Reading and parsing the files: 0.8 to 1.0 ms of Chakra's `Button` first answer (about 470 ms), whose union props are declared in 83 KB of Chakra's `system.gen.d.ts` and @types/react's 183 KB `index.d.ts`. On gate-large, peak RSS 610 to 616 MB against 608 to 612, and the same CPU time (two runs each).
240	- **Gate.** Both lanes compare `default` and member order on every row; the checker lane runs with `--no-resolver-facts` and passes every row. Rows `objects/41` to `43` (a destructured default, `defaultProps`, a code default over a different `@default`) and `literals/35` (a type literal's union) cover what a single-file row can; a union through an import needs the cross-file rows of S7b.
241	
242	## TypeScript 7.1 API
243	
244	| Topic | Detail |
245	| --- | --- |
246	| Where | `microsoft/TypeScript` `main` (`7.1.0-dev`). typescript-go closed on 2026-08-20 |
247	| Timeline | The plan ([#63703](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/63703)) put the beta on 2026-10-06; npm published `7.1.0-beta` on 2026-10-20. RC 2026-11-10 and stable 2026-11-24 are still planned |
248	| Get it | `npm i typescript@beta` (`7.1.0-beta`) or `@next` (daily `7.1.0-dev`). 7.0.x (`latest`, `7.0.2`) has no API |
249	| Launch | `tsc --api [--async] --cwd <dir> --useCaseSensitiveFileNames=<bool>`, plus `--runExternalCode` and `--timing` when asked. With `--async`: JSON-RPC with LSP-style `Content-Length` framing over stdio (`vscode-jsonrpc`), handled concurrently. Without it: msgpack over stdio |
250	| msgpack caveats | Each message is a 3-element msgpack array: message type (u8), method (bin) and payload (bin). The server answers one request at a time, so a sync client blocks until the reply. Encoded strings are WTF-8: a lone surrogate from a JS string survives, so a Rust client must not decode them as strict UTF-8 |
251	| Stability | The beta's JS entry points are `typescript/sync`, `/async`, `/proto`, `/ast` and `/ast/*`, `/fs`, `/path` and `/vscode`; the root export is only the version. The `unstable/*` names in ADR 0006 were the nightlies' and are gone. The protocol has no version handshake, so pin the build |
252	| Positions | UTF-16 code units. OXC offsets are UTF-8 bytes |
253	| Surface | 177 methods in `7.1.0-beta` (`APIMethodInfo` in `dist/api/proto.generated.d.ts`), up from 157 on 2026-09-19, mostly with TS 6 checker names. Every call in "The algorithm" is present |
254	
255	**Beta re-probe (2026-10-21, `7.1.0-beta`).** `crates/tsc-client`'s smoke example spawned the beta's `bin/tsc --api`, completed the `initialize` round trip (`caseSensitivity`, `currentDirectory`) and shut down cleanly with exit status 0, so framing and shutdown behave as the fake-tsc harness assumes. `TSC_PACKAGE_DIR=<dir> cargo run -p caliper-docgen-tsc-client --example smoke_real_tsc` repeats it against any installed `typescript`. The beta's `proto.generated.d.ts` still exposes every checker call the algorithm uses: `getTypeAtLocation`, `getTypeOfSymbol`, `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol`, `getSignaturesOfType`, `getResolvedSignature`, `getReturnTypeOfSignature`, `getBaseTypes` and `getPropertiesOfType`. The fixture-corpus parity run below was re-run on the beta on 2026-10-23 (`apps/oracle` imports `typescript-beta`, `npm:typescript@7.1.0-beta`, since the `unstable/*` entry points are gone). Two beta behaviors to know: the server panics (`interface conversion: interface {} is string, not float64`) when `createProgram` gets string-valued enum options such as `target: 'es2022'`, so pass options from `parseConfigFile`; and `true`/`false` literal types carry neither `value` nor `intrinsicName`, so read them with `typeToString`. Discovery over a whole project ran in the oracle: 33 to 1,531 components per corpus.
256	
257	**Churn.** About 20 commits touched the protocol definition (`proto.go`) between 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-18. `updateSnapshot`, project IDs and `createProgram` params were reshaped on 09-17 and 09-18. Every call the algorithm uses ran unchanged on the 09-20 and 09-26 nightlies. Re-verify on the beta.
258	
259	**Freshness.** tsc sees an edit to a dependency only when told:
260	
261	```js
262	const s1 = await s0.update({ fileNotifications: { changed: [file] }, ensurePrograms: true })
263	```
264	
265	With the notification, the dependent component's props updated (0.5 ms update, 2.8 ms query). An unnotified disk edit stayed stale (2026-09-20). Both incremental paths now notify it (`WatchSession::update_file` and `WatchSession::ensure_fresh`), and an edit neither saw is caught before an answer: see "Watch" above.
266	
267	## Evidence
268	
269	Method: RDT 2.4.0 on typescript@6.0.3 (`apps/oracle`'s RDT is pinned to a TS6 API — see "The RDT oracle" below) with the harness options (`shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`, `propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false }`), against the algorithm above on the nightly named in each row, or `7.1.0-beta`. The harness that ran it is not in the repository: the table is the record.
270	
271	| Check | Result | Nightly |
272	| --- | --- | --- |
273	| 13 components: the 10 outliers, base-ui `MenuRoot`, shadcn `Button`, mui `Button` | 0 missing and 0 extra props. `required` 3412/3412. Type strings 3410/3412 | 09-26 |
274	| Descriptions: ariakit, MUI, fluentui, shadcn | 294/294, 311/311, 288/288, 292/292 | 09-20 |
275	| `parent`: ariakit `MenuButton` | 294/294 in 12 requests | 09-20 |
276	| Fixture corpus, 55 files in one program | 70 components in common, equal prop counts on 70/70 | 09-20 |
277	| Class components | 2/2 on a synthetic file. The corpus has none | 09-20 |
278	| Full fixture corpus, 44 files / 47 components / 5554 props, one program | 5 missing, 27 extra. `required` 5508/5522. Type strings 5265/5522. Descriptions 47/47 | 09-26 |
279	| The same run | 5 missing, 27 extra. `required` 5508/5522. Type strings 5266/5522. Descriptions 47/47. Of the 13 components above, the two nested `ref` unions and ark-ui `SelectRoot.ids` differ | `7.1.0-beta` |
280	
281	Type strings match after two normalizations. tsc prints union members in internal type-id order, which differs from TS 5.9, so members are compared as a set. RDT also runs `.replace(' | undefined', '')` twice, which turns a nested `=> string | undefined` into `=> string` and loses information. Canonical output keeps it. The 2 remaining differences are nested `ref` unions in fluentui and base-ui.
282	
283	Of the corpus's 26 RDT-only entries, 23 have no props and 3 are default exports RDT names differently (mui `Button` confirmed at 311/311).
284	
285	The full-corpus run's 257 remaining mismatches, unlike the curated 13, aren't all real algorithm gaps:
286	
287	- Most are non-component exports the "single-parameter function" heuristic sweeps in — plain string-returning helpers (`antd/buttonHelpers.ts`, `headlessui/render.ts`'s `mergeProps`, `blueprint/blueprintTypes.ts`) whose "props" are `String.prototype`/`Array.prototype` members. RDT is equally permissive and picks these up too, so both tools agree these aren't components; the mismatches are TS 6 vs TS 7.1-dev lib.d.ts differences (e.g. `padStart`'s parameter renamed `maxLength`→`targetLength`) and per-run `Symbol.iterator` id suffixes, not a resolver bug.

- **Measured** (`extract` with the checker, then behind `--experimental-semantic-types`, with the weekly's options, tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, against the run before this slice). Before, the structural answer gave the order of 2,736 of Spectrum's 3,194 merged union props and 187 of gate-large's 432,813, and every default: on Spectrum 870 from code, 378 `@default` tags the checker also gives, 15 from the resolver only; on gate-large 499 tags. Now, Spectrum: 27 props gain a code default and none loses one; 11 of 3,686 unions change order, each to the written one (`focusMode?: 'child' | 'cell'`, `slot?: string | null`). With `--no-resolver-facts` 15 defaults (the mapped `@default` case above) and 22 more union orders (imported aliases) differ. gate-large: 834 props gain a default (the checker's `@default` tags of props only the checker returns) and none loses one; 1,452 of 432,690 unions take the written order (`translate?: 'yes' | 'no'`, `css`); with `--no-resolver-facts` no default and 16 more union orders differ (members through an import, such as MUI's `timeout?: TransitionProps['timeout'] | 'auto'`).
- **Cost.** Reading and parsing the files: 0.8 to 1.0 ms of Chakra's `Button` first answer (about 470 ms), whose union props are declared in 83 KB of Chakra's `system.gen.d.ts` and @types/react's 183 KB `index.d.ts`. On gate-large, peak RSS 610 to 616 MB against 608 to 612, and the same CPU time (two runs each).
- **Gate.** Both lanes compare `default` and member order on every row; the checker lane runs with `--no-resolver-facts` and passes every row. Rows `objects/41` to `43` (a destructured default, `defaultProps`, a code default over a different `@default`) and `literals/35` (a type literal's union) cover what a single-file row can; a union through an import needs the cross-file rows of S7b.

## TypeScript 7.1 API

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Where | `microsoft/TypeScript` `main` (`7.1.0-dev`). typescript-go closed on 2026-08-20 |
| Timeline | The plan ([#63703](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/63703)) put the beta on 2026-10-06; npm published `7.1.0-beta` on 2026-10-20. RC 2026-11-10 and stable 2026-11-24 are still planned |
| Get it | `npm i typescript@beta` (`7.1.0-beta`) or `@next` (daily `7.1.0-dev`). 7.0.x (`latest`, `7.0.2`) has no API |
| Launch | `tsc --api [--async] --cwd <dir> --useCaseSensitiveFileNames=<bool>`, plus `--runExternalCode` and `--timing` when asked. With `--async`: JSON-RPC with LSP-style `Content-Length` framing over stdio (`vscode-jsonrpc`), handled concurrently. Without it: msgpack over stdio |
| msgpack caveats | Each message is a 3-element msgpack array: message type (u8), method (bin) and payload (bin). The server answers one request at a time, so a sync client blocks until the reply. Encoded strings are WTF-8: a lone surrogate from a JS string survives, so a Rust client must not decode them as strict UTF-8 |
| Stability | The beta's JS entry points are `typescript/sync`, `/async`, `/proto`, `/ast` and `/ast/*`, `/fs`, `/path` and `/vscode`; the root export is only the version. The `unstable/*` names in ADR 0006 were the nightlies' and are gone. The protocol has no version handshake, so pin the build |
| Positions | UTF-16 code units. OXC offsets are UTF-8 bytes |
| Surface | 177 methods in `7.1.0-beta` (`APIMethodInfo` in `dist/api/proto.generated.d.ts`), up from 157 on 2026-09-19, mostly with TS 6 checker names. Every call in "The algorithm" is present |

**Beta re-probe (2026-10-21, `7.1.0-beta`).** `crates/tsc-client`'s smoke example spawned the beta's `bin/tsc --api`, completed the `initialize` round trip (`caseSensitivity`, `currentDirectory`) and shut down cleanly with exit status 0, so framing and shutdown behave as the fake-tsc harness assumes. `TSC_PACKAGE_DIR=<dir> cargo run -p caliper-docgen-tsc-client --example smoke_real_tsc` repeats it against any installed `typescript`. The beta's `proto.generated.d.ts` still exposes every checker call the algorithm uses: `getTypeAtLocation`, `getTypeOfSymbol`, `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol`, `getSignaturesOfType`, `getResolvedSignature`, `getReturnTypeOfSignature`, `getBaseTypes` and `getPropertiesOfType`. The fixture-corpus parity run below was re-run on the beta on 2026-10-23 (`apps/oracle` imports `typescript-beta`, `npm:typescript@7.1.0-beta`, since the `unstable/*` entry points are gone). Two beta behaviors to know: the server panics (`interface conversion: interface {} is string, not float64`) when `createProgram` gets string-valued enum options such as `target: 'es2022'`, so pass options from `parseConfigFile`; and `true`/`false` literal types carry neither `value` nor `intrinsicName`, so read them with `typeToString`. Discovery over a whole project ran in the oracle: 33 to 1,531 components per corpus.

**Churn.** About 20 commits touched the protocol definition (`proto.go`) between 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-18. `updateSnapshot`, project IDs and `createProgram` params were reshaped on 09-17 and 09-18. Every call the algorithm uses ran unchanged on the 09-20 and 09-26 nightlies. Re-verify on the beta.

**Freshness.** tsc sees an edit to a dependency only when told:

```js
const s1 = await s0.update({ fileNotifications: { changed: [file] }, ensurePrograms: true })
```

With the notification, the dependent component's props updated (0.5 ms update, 2.8 ms query). An unnotified disk edit stayed stale (2026-09-20). Both incremental paths now notify it (`WatchSession::update_file` and `WatchSession::ensure_fresh`), and an edit neither saw is caught before an answer: see "Watch" above.

## Evidence

Method: RDT 2.4.0 on typescript@6.0.3 (`apps/oracle`'s RDT is pinned to a TS6 API — see "The RDT oracle" below) with the harness options (`shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`, `propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false }`), against the algorithm above on the nightly named in each row, or `7.1.0-beta`. The harness that ran it is not in the repository: the table is the record.

| Check | Result | Nightly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13 components: the 10 outliers, base-ui `MenuRoot`, shadcn `Button`, mui `Button` | 0 missing and 0 extra props. `required` 3412/3412. Type strings 3410/3412 | 09-26 |
| Descriptions: ariakit, MUI, fluentui, shadcn | 294/294, 311/311, 288/288, 292/292 | 09-20 |
| `parent`: ariakit `MenuButton` | 294/294 in 12 requests | 09-20 |
| Fixture corpus, 55 files in one program | 70 components in common, equal prop counts on 70/70 | 09-20 |
| Class components | 2/2 on a synthetic file. The corpus has none | 09-20 |
| Full fixture corpus, 44 files / 47 components / 5554 props, one program | 5 missing, 27 extra. `required` 5508/5522. Type strings 5265/5522. Descriptions 47/47 | 09-26 |
| The same run | 5 missing, 27 extra. `required` 5508/5522. Type strings 5266/5522. Descriptions 47/47. Of the 13 components above, the two nested `ref` unions and ark-ui `SelectRoot.ids` differ | `7.1.0-beta` |

- Most are non-component exports the "single-parameter function" heuristic sweeps in — plain string-returning helpers (`antd/buttonHelpers.ts`, `headlessui/render.ts`'s `mergeProps`, `blueprint/blueprintTypes.ts`) whose "props" are `String.prototype`/`Array.prototype` members. The owner's decision (2026-11-12): the checker answers by default on every surface, the whole-project `extract` included, though its default no longer has the structural resolver's speed. One name per concept: `--no-checker` on the command line, `checker: false` in `docgen.config.ts`, the napi options and the Storybook addon. `--experimental-semantic-types`, the config's `experimentalSemanticTypes` and `semanticTypes` are removed: the CLI and the config refuse them as unknown, and the addon refuses `semanticTypes` by name, since left unread `semanticTypes: 'off'` would quietly run the checker.

# caliper-docgen

Extract React component props from the command line. Built on [OXC](https://oxc.rs), so there is no type-checking pass.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen
npx caliper-docgen extract --src src --format rdt
```

| Command               | Does                                                                 |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `extract`             | Writes every component's props to stdout or `--out`                  |
| `watch`               | Re-extracts on change                                                |
| `inspect <Component>` | Shows one component's props as a table                               |
| `check`               | Exits non-zero on errors, for CI (`--strict` also fails on warnings) |
| `schema`              | Prints the JSON Schema of the output                                 |

`--format` is `canonical`, `rdt` (the `react-docgen-typescript` shape) or `toon` (compact, for LLM agents). Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts`, or in the file passed with `--config`.

This package is a thin wrapper. It runs the prebuilt binary for your platform, installed as an optional dependency (`caliper-docgen-darwin-arm64`, `caliper-docgen-linux-x64-gnu`, and so on). All behavior is in the Rust CLI.

Docs, benchmarks and migration notes: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT. Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.
# caliper-docgen

Extract React component props from the command line. Built on [OXC](https://oxc.rs), so there is no type-checking pass.

```bash
cargo install caliper-docgen
caliper-docgen extract --src src --format rdt
```

| Command               | Does                                                                 |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `extract`             | Writes every component's props to stdout or `--out`                  |
| `watch`               | Re-extracts on change                                                |
| `inspect <Component>` | Shows one component's props as a table                               |
| `check`               | Exits non-zero on errors, for CI (`--strict` also fails on warnings) |
| `schema`              | Prints the JSON Schema of the output                                 |

`--format` is `canonical`, `rdt` (the `react-docgen-typescript` shape) or `toon` (compact, for LLM agents). Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts`, or in the file passed with `--config`.

Prefer npm? `npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen` installs the same binary.

Extraction is in [`caliper-docgen-core`](https://crates.io/crates/caliper-docgen-core). Docs, benchmarks and migration notes: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

[FSL-1.1-MIT](LICENSE). Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.
# caliper-docgen-core

The extraction library behind [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper). It reads React components from TypeScript with [OXC](https://oxc.rs) and reports their props, with no TypeScript compiler program and no type-checking pass.

It parses files in parallel, merges symbols across them, and resolves each component's props. When it can't resolve something it returns a `Diagnostic` instead of failing silently. There is no terminal output and no async, so it embeds cleanly.

Most people want a front end instead: the [`caliper-docgen`](https://crates.io/crates/caliper-docgen) CLI, or the Node bindings [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi).

API docs: [docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core](https://docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core). Project page: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source and architecture notes: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

# caliper-docgen-napi

Node.js bindings for [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper), so JavaScript can call the extractor directly.

```bash
npm install caliper-docgen-napi
```

The prebuilt addon for your OS and CPU installs as an optional dependency (`caliper-docgen-napi-darwin-arm64`, `caliper-docgen-napi-linux-x64-gnu`, and so on).

Most projects want [`caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-vite-plugin) or the [`caliper-docgen`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen) CLI, which use this package. The binding returns the canonical output format; a session also gives each component's `__docgenInfo` in the `react-docgen-typescript` shape (`RdtComponentDoc` in `index.d.ts`).

Project page: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT. Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `srcDirs` | `['src']` | Directories to extract from, relative to Storybook's working directory. |
| `exclude` |  | Glob patterns to skip, gitignore-style and relative to each source directory: `**/*.fixture.tsx`, `legacy/`. A bare name such as `Button` matches only a file or folder named exactly that. |
| `tsconfigPath` |  | tsconfig for path aliases. |
| `skipHtmlProps` | `false` | Leave out the HTML attributes a component inherits from its element. |
| `htmlAttributes` | `full` | `full` lists all of the HTML attributes, `curated` a compact subset (handlers, `aria-*`, `ref`, common attributes), `none` none. Wins over `skipHtmlProps`. |
| `cache` | `true` | Read and write the on-disk caches under `node_modules/.cache`. `false` reads and writes nothing there and parses everything every run; the output is the same. |
| `loadDependencies` | `true` | Read the type declarations your props reference from installed packages, so library-typed props resolve instead of degrading. `false` skips the work. |
| `collapseInheritedProps` | `none` | `none` lists every inherited prop. `dependencies` lists large ambient dependency sources (DOM and ARIA attributes, style systems) as one layer of names; `all` also does so for project sources of more than 30 props. |
| `lazy` | `true` | Resolve a component when a story asks for it. `false` resolves every component at start; the answers are the same. |
| `fillAfter` | `0` | With `lazy`, once this many distinct components were asked for, resolve the rest in the background in one parallel pass. It lowers the median story latency of a project read end to end (Spectrum's 50 stories: 19 ms to 5 ms) but not the total time, and raises peak memory by 170 to 420 MB, so it is off. `16` is a reasonable value to try. |
| `warmUp` | `false` | With `lazy`, resolve a few components in the background after start. Off: it did not make the first story faster in measurement. |
| `prefetchStories` | `1` | When `storybook dev` starts, document the components of this many first stories through Storybook's docgen service before a browser asks, one after another. That starts the session (and the checker), and stores the opening story's answer where the browser reads it: with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, Chakra's `Button` had the checker's props in the browser before it asked, where they arrived 0.7 to 2.9 s after its request without. The browser still asks the provider again, which answers from the session. A story opened while a prefetch runs waits for it, so a larger number only pays off when the browser opens later than the components take. `0` waits for the browser. |
| `semanticTypes` | `'off'` | Experimental. `'on-demand'` keeps the built-in TypeScript 7.1 checker warm and asks it for the component a story shows, so props only the type checker can see appear (shadcn's components gain more than twice as many). A story waits up to `semanticWaitMs` for it and otherwise shows the usual props; the checker's answer is kept for the next request. The checker answers the stories you open before `warmUp` and `fillAfter` work, and a story whose component it is already answering waits for that answer instead of asking again. Nothing to install: the checker is part of the addon's native binding. |
| `tscPath` | the built-in checker | A checker binary for `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` to run instead: `typescript@7.1`'s `tsc`, or `tsrs`. |
| `semanticWaitMs` | `150` | How many milliseconds a story waits for the checker before it takes the usual props. |
| `semanticWaitEmptyMs` | `2000` | How many milliseconds a story waits for the checker when caliper-docgen's own pass lists no props for its component (for example `ComponentProps<typeof Button>` of a library it cannot read), since there is nothing to show before the checker answers. A value below `semanticWaitMs` gives such a story `semanticWaitMs`. |
| `fallback` | `degraded` | `degraded`: a component whose extraction reported a warning or error goes to React's docgen; a prop it could only report as opaque (an `info` diagnostic) does not, and shows its type text with an `object` control. Once the checker answers for a component, a warning about what its answer replaces (a component caliper-docgen could not find, a type it could not resolve) no longer counts; one about what the checker could not read either still does. `never`: always answer. |

A story whose component caliper-docgen can't find goes to React's docgen, which stays registered underneath. Each component handed on is logged once as a warning with the reason (the extraction diagnostics that affect it).

The defaults favour completeness over Storybook's: caliper-docgen is fast enough to read dependency types and list inherited props that a checker-backed docgen leaves out.

## Differences from React's docgen

React's docgen in Storybook 11 asks the TypeScript checker for each component. On the same components, the argTypes differ in two ways:

- A string default keeps caliper-docgen's quotes: `"md"` where React's docgen shows the source text, `'md'`.
- Type text is printed as written: `MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>` where the checker prints `MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement, MouseEvent>`, and `{ date?: string }` where it prints `{ date?: string | undefined; }`.
# caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

// A component lists the ids of its prop sets; a prop set maps each prop name to a prop id, and each distinct prop is
// written once, in `docgen.props`.
const [firstSetId] = docgen.components['Button'].props
const label = docgen.props[docgen.propSets[firstSetId].label]
```

On every change the virtual module reloads with the same output a fresh extraction would give, including removed components, enums and diagnostics. To apply changes yourself, listen for the update event:

```ts
import.meta.hot?.on(

# caliper-docgen-core

The extraction library behind [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper). It reads React components from TypeScript with [OXC](https://oxc.rs) and reports their props, with no TypeScript compiler program and no type-checking pass.

It parses files in parallel, merges symbols across them, and resolves each component's props. When it can't resolve something it returns a `Diagnostic` instead of failing silently. There is no terminal output and no async, so it embeds cleanly.

Most people want a front end instead: the [`caliper-docgen`](https://crates.io/crates/caliper-docgen) CLI, or the Node bindings [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi).

API docs: [docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core](https://docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core). Project page: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source and architecture notes: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

# caliper-docgen-napi

Node.js bindings for [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper), so JavaScript can call the extractor directly.

```bash
npm install caliper-docgen-napi
```

The prebuilt addon for your OS and CPU installs as an optional dependency (`caliper-docgen-napi-darwin-arm64`, `caliper-docgen-napi-linux-x64-gnu`, and so on).

Most projects want [`caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-vite-plugin) or the [`caliper-docgen`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen) CLI, which use this package. The binding returns the canonical output format; a session also gives each component's `__docgenInfo` in the `react-docgen-typescript` shape (`RdtComponentDoc` in `index.d.ts`).

Project page: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `srcDirs` | `['src']` | Directories to extract from, relative to Storybook's working directory. |
| `exclude` |  | Glob patterns to skip, gitignore-style and relative to each source directory: `**/*.fixture.tsx`, `legacy/`. A bare name such as `Button` matches only a file or folder named exactly that. |
| `tsconfigPath` |  | tsconfig for path aliases. |
| `skipHtmlProps` | `false` | Leave out the HTML attributes a component inherits from its element. |
| `htmlAttributes` | `full` | `full` lists all of the HTML attributes, `curated` a compact subset (handlers, `aria-*`, `ref`, common attributes), `none` none. Wins over `skipHtmlProps`. |
| `cache` | `true` | Read and write the on-disk caches under `node_modules/.cache`. `false` reads and writes nothing there and parses everything every run; the output is the same. |
| `loadDependencies` | `true` | Read the type declarations your props reference from installed packages, so library-typed props resolve instead of degrading. `false` skips the work. |
| `collapseInheritedProps` | `none` | `none` lists every inherited prop. `dependencies` lists large ambient dependency sources (DOM and ARIA attributes, style systems) as one layer of names; `all` also does so for project sources of more than 30 props. |
| `lazy` | `true` | Resolve a component when a story asks for it. `false` resolves every component at start; the answers are the same. |
| `fillAfter` | `0` | With `lazy`, once this many distinct components were asked for, resolve the rest in the background in one parallel pass. It lowers the median story latency of a project read end to end (Spectrum's 50 stories: 19 ms to 5 ms) but not the total time, and raises peak memory by 170 to 420 MB, so it is off. `16` is a reasonable value to try. |
| `warmUp` | `false` | With `lazy`, resolve a few components in the background after start. Off: it did not make the first story faster in measurement. |
| `prefetchStories` | `1` | When `storybook dev` starts, document the components of this many first stories through Storybook's docgen service before a browser asks, one after another. That starts the session (and the checker), and stores the opening story's answer where the browser reads it: with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, Chakra's `Button` had the checker's props in the browser before it asked, where they arrived 0.7 to 2.9 s after its request without. The browser still asks the provider again, which answers from the session. A story opened while a prefetch runs waits for it, so a larger number only pays off when the browser opens later than the components take. `0` waits for the browser. |
| `semanticTypes` | `'off'` | Experimental. `'on-demand'` keeps the built-in TypeScript 7.1 checker warm and asks it for the component a story shows, so props only the type checker can see appear (shadcn's components gain more than twice as many). A story waits up to `semanticWaitMs` for it and otherwise shows the usual props; the checker's answer is kept for the next request. The checker answers the stories you open before `warmUp` and `fillAfter` work, and a story whose component it is already answering waits for that answer instead of asking again. Nothing to install: the checker is part of the addon's native binding. |
| `tscPath` | the built-in checker | A checker binary for `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` to run instead: `typescript@7.1`'s `tsc`, or `tsrs`. |
| `semanticWaitMs` | `150` | How many milliseconds a story waits for the checker before it takes the usual props. |
| `semanticWaitEmptyMs` | `2000` | How many milliseconds a story waits for the checker when caliper-docgen's own pass lists no props for its component (for example `ComponentProps<typeof Button>` of a library it cannot read), since there is nothing to show before the checker answers. A value below `semanticWaitMs` gives such a story `semanticWaitMs`. |
| `fallback` | `degraded` | `degraded`: a component whose extraction reported a warning or error goes to React's docgen; a prop it could only report as opaque (an `info` diagnostic) does not, and shows its type text with an `object` control. Once the checker answers for a component, a warning about what its answer replaces (a component caliper-docgen could not find, a type it could not resolve) no longer counts; one about what the checker could not read either still does. `never`: always answer. |

A story whose component caliper-docgen can't find goes to React's docgen, which stays registered underneath. Each component handed on is logged once as a warning with the reason (the extraction diagnostics that affect it).

The defaults favour completeness over Storybook's: caliper-docgen is fast enough to read dependency types and list inherited props that a checker-backed docgen leaves out.

## Differences from React's docgen

React's docgen in Storybook 11 asks the TypeScript checker for each component. On the same components, the argTypes differ in two ways:

- A string default keeps caliper-docgen's quotes: `"md"` where React's docgen shows the source text, `'md'`.
- Type text is printed as written: `MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>` where the checker prints `MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement, MouseEvent>`, and `{ date?: string }` where it prints `{ date?: string | undefined; }`.
# caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})

import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

// A component lists the ids of its prop sets; a prop set maps each prop name to a prop id, and each distinct prop is
// written once, in `docgen.props`.
const [firstSetId] = docgen.components['Button'].props

)
